terminal.description: The route board runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. This shell is in your workspace if you want to look around, for example at data/routes.json.

tasks.title: Load the routes from the file
tasks.description:
The office now writes the real route list to `data/routes.json` every night. Load the board from it: - fetch `data/routes.json` with a path relative to the page and read the JSON - before you fetch, show the `

` line (it starts hidden) with a sentence that says the routes are loading, for example `Loading routes...` - once the routes arrive, hide `#board-status`, draw the board and the count The old array in `src/routes.js` should no longer be used. A good shape is an `async` function in `src/routes.js` that returns the routes, called from `src/main.js`. Search, ticks and the form keep working with the loaded routes.
nextSteps: Open `data/routes.json` and compare it with the old array.
Write an async function in `src/routes.js` that fetches the file and returns the parsed routes.
In `main.js`, keep the routes in a variable that starts empty and fill it once they arrive.
Show the loading line first, then hide it and call `render()` after the routes are in.
hints: The board cannot be drawn at load time any more, because the routes are not there yet. Drawing has to wait for them.
`fetch` gives a response, and `await response.json()` gives the data. Both need `await` inside an `async` function.
`routes` in `main.js` has to change once the data arrives, so it can no longer be an import. Use `let routes = []` and assign the loaded array to it before rendering.

tasks.title: Say when the routes cannot load
tasks.description:
Sometimes the file is missing or the network is down. Then `#board-status` stays visible with a line that contains `Could not load` (any letter case), for example `Could not load the routes. Check the connection and reload the page.`

This covers two cases the check tries:

- the server answers with an error status such as 500
- `fetch` itself fails

No error should escape to the console in either case.
nextSteps: Rename `data/routes.json` for a moment and look at the board. Put the name back after.
Check `response.ok` after the fetch and throw when it is false.
Wrap the loading in `try` and `catch` in `main.js`.
In the `catch`, put the failure sentence in `#board-status`.
hints: `fetch` only rejects when no answer came back at all. A 404 or 500 is still an answer.
Throwing your own error for a bad status lets one `catch` handle both cases.
In the `catch`, change the text of the line that already says loading. Leave it visible and skip drawing the board.

tasks.title: Remember ticks overnight
tasks.description:
Write `loadTicks()` and `saveTicks(ticked)` in `src/store.js`, and use them in `src/main.js`.

- the ticked route ids are saved in `localStorage` under the key `gritstone-ticks`, as a JSON array of ids
- they are saved after every tick and every untick
- on load the saved ids come back, so those routes show ticked
- the count only counts routes that are on the board, even if the save holds old ids
- when the saved value is missing or is not valid JSON, the board loads with nothing ticked
nextSteps: Tick a route, reload the Browser panel and see the tick disappear.
In `saveTicks`, turn the set into an array and save it as JSON.
In `loadTicks`, read the key, parse it and turn it back into a `Set`.
Use both in `main.js`: load once at the start, save in the tick handler.
hints: `localStorage` only stores strings. A `Set` needs to become an array and then JSON on the way in, and go the other way on the way out.
`JSON.parse` throws on text that is not JSON, and `getItem` gives `null` for a key that was never saved.
`[...ticked]` makes an array from a set and `new Set(array)` goes back. Wrap the parse in `try` and return an empty set from the `catch`.
